Earlier this summer, in early July, Apple added a basic search feature update to its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be widely welcomed by users, but the same TestFlight update introduced an extremely annoying bug for many users.

As for me, I was not noticeably affected by this bug, so at the time I thought the TestFlight update was a simple but important step forward.

Sometimes a small change can have a major impact. For users who have accumulated a large backlog of pre-loaded software, Apple's latest TestFlight update perfectly illustrates this point. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac and other platforms, with the new version 4.3 adding "a search field to help you quickly find relevant apps."

Looking back, I actually did notice some strange situations, which I mentioned at the end of the article (although my judgment was completely the opposite):

I suspect the reason I did not notice this so-called bug is that two years ago I "merged" several TestFlight accounts I had been using for years into my iCloud and App Store Apple account. Although the process was extremely tedious, it was worth it for me.

Regardless, the TestFlight bug did not escape the sharp eyes of MacStories' John Vorhees:

So, you can imagine how excited I was when I saw Zac Hall's article on 9to5Mac saying that TestFlight had finally added a search bar. I thought to myself: "Finally." I immediately stopped what I was doing and updated the app. [...] Unfortunately, there is a huge "however" here. In the past, TestFlight's beta versions were arranged in reverse chronological order, and I personally really liked this arrangement. [...] Now the expired beta versions are scattered among the active betas arranged in alphabetical order, and the list of expired betas seems to have even expanded to include every beta I had ever participated in. I did a rough count—it's almost 800 app entries for me. If you can imagine, the number of truly active betas among them is very small. The search function is certainly helpful, but it's no longer possible to find things by scrolling.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote an article on Daring Fireball about the TestFlight update and this bug:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was pointed out by Vorhees), Apple finally released an update for TestFlight. Although the update notes only mention bug fixes, this update does indeed correct the relevant bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is a fix targeting this regression issue.
